intro: Improvements are separated into what this pass already implemented and what is waiting for your decision. Nothing marked 'awaiting your choice' has been built, so the site's behaviour matches what is on screen.

implemented_this_pass.title: Trip-cost calculator (entries x buy-ins + nights x true nightly)
implemented_this_pass.detail: On the Trip cost page, pre-filled from the plan builder; every input carries its own source link and state, and unverified inputs are marked rather than guessed.

implemented_this_pass.title: Search box across every table
implemented_this_pass.detail: One search field per page filters the visible tables; a global search box on the landing page jumps to the matching page and row.

implemented_this_pass.title: Date filter
implemented_this_pass.detail: From/to date inputs on the events and schedule tables, plus single-day presets for the recommended windows.

implemented_this_pass.title: Single-entry / freezeout toggle
implemented_this_pass.detail: Three-state filter (candidate, not stated, excluded) wired to the sheet evidence, with the definition shown next to the control.

implemented_this_pass.title: Walking <=30 min filter
implemented_this_pass.detail: Implemented and honest: with zero verified durations it returns 'no verified rows', which is the correct answer, not an empty accident.

implemented_this_pass.title: One page per venue with its events and hotels
implemented_this_pass.detail: Venetian, Wynn, Caesars/Horseshoe, MGM Grand, Bellagio, ARIA, Golden Nugget, each with its coverage state and what is still missing.

implemented_this_pass.title: Last-checked date on every row
implemented_this_pass.detail: Each event, hotel field and source row carries the date the value was read and whether it was read in this pass.

implemented_this_pass.title: Rates kept as a dated log
implemented_this_pass.detail: site-data/rates.json appends entries; nothing overwrites a previous quote, and each entry states the dates it applied to.

implemented_this_pass.title: Automatic re-check of each official URL
implemented_this_pass.detail: GitHub Actions cron (daily 06:30 UTC) fetches every official source, hashes it, extracts the 34 tracked values, compares them field by field and publishes a change report; changed sources mark their rows on the site. The extractor has an offline self-test that both workflows run first, and snapshot-only churn is never committed - only a real signal, which opens a review PR instead of editing data silently.

implemented_this_pass.title: Morning schedule scrape
implemented_this_pass.detail: The same job re-parses the Venetian schedule page into a machine-readable snapshot and reports any row it cannot parse instead of guessing.

implemented_this_pass.title: Overlap / feasibility flags and per-day primary + conditional fallback
implemented_this_pass.detail: Computed from published start times, registration cutoffs and level lengths; the formula is printed next to the table.

implemented_this_pass.title: Structured rule fields with excerpts
implemented_this_pass.detail: single_entry, re_entry, add_on, fee, guarantee, payout and bounty are stored per event, each with status (explicit / not stated after full read / not read), verbatim excerpt, source URL and retrieval date.

implemented_this_pass.title: Ranking discipline
implemented_this_pass.detail: Ranking only uses rows whose fee and guarantee are both confirmed; bounty and flight events are labelled and separated, and the guarantee/buy-in number is described as a size ratio, never a forecast.

implemented_this_pass.title: One coordination board, one canonical site
implemented_this_pass.detail: Duplicate dashboards retired (FG-16); COORDINATION.md is the single shared board.

implemented_this_pass.title: Read the remaining 27 structure sheets - DONE 2026-11-17
implemented_this_pass.detail: Completed by arena/18aba6dd-poker2: all 27 remaining official sheets (2, 3, 4, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19-28, 30-37) were read in full on 2026-11-17 and transcribed with verbatim excerpts. Result: 45 single-entry candidate rows, 0 unverified Venetian rows, and new findings - LIPS events withhold an extra flat fee ($10 of $600 for events 35/43, $20 of $800 for event 39), the $600 Seniors sheets pay 15% of the field, event 39 is one starting day + Day 2 (not multi-flight), and events 56/59 publish early-registration rake discounts ($40/$20 off the first entry before start). The written single-entry confirmation from the room (Q-03) remains outstanding.

implemented_this_pass.title: Add a routing source for walking durations - DONE 2026-11-17
implemented_this_pass.detail: Completed without an API key: official addresses geocoded via OpenStreetMap Nominatim and foot-routed with the OSRM foot profile on the public FOSSGIS server (routing.openstreetmap.de/routed-foot). All 12 hotel-to-venue pairs now carry routed minutes (10 reused from the 2026-11-16 measurement dataset, 2 measured fresh), each with Google/Apple Maps confirmation links. Routed minutes are estimates, not official measurements - the Hotels page labels them as such. Park MGM (34 min) and ARIA (30.6 min) fail the 30-minute rule; the other pairs pass.

awaiting_your_choice.title: Lock the trip dates
awaiting_your_choice.why: It unblocks the checkout-total capture (Q-08), the 30-minute walk test on the actual route in that weather, and the room-rate comparison; today every date-dependent field is blank by design.

awaiting_your_choice.title: Add the other Strip rooms one venue per run
awaiting_your_choice.what: Same three-state method for Bellagio, Caesars Palace, Horseshoe, MGM Grand, ARIA, then downtown.
awaiting_your_choice.why: Today the ranking covers one poker room; the user brief says 'Strip', and a cheaper single-entry freezeout could exist at Bellagio on a Friday.

awaiting_your_choice.title: Pick a quality source for hotels
awaiting_your_choice.what: Either accept a named third-party rating system as an allowed source class, or drop quality from the model and rank on cost plus fee certainty only.
awaiting_your_choice.why: The brief ranks quality above distance, but official pages publish no comparable tier; without a rule here the quality column stays empty (FG-12).

awaiting_your_choice.title: Allow the exact-date itemised quote in
awaiting_your_choice.what: Paste the booking engine's itemisation for your dates into the rate log (or approve a serverless fetch of the published rate feed).
awaiting_your_choice.why: This is the single missing number in true-cost-per-night; everything else in the formula is already verified (FG-05).
awaiting_your_choice.effort: two minutes in the booking flow

awaiting_your_choice.title: Get single-entry answers in writing
awaiting_your_choice.what: One email to the poker desk for the events in your plan; store the reply as a source row with the date.
awaiting_your_choice.why: The only path from 'no contrary clause' to 'confirmed single-entry' (FG-02).

awaiting_your_choice.title: Add a bankroll cap and an entry-count limit to the planner
awaiting_your_choice.what: Cap total buy-ins per trip and per day, with the schedule builder refusing to exceed it.
awaiting_your_choice.why: Maximising entries and guarantee exposure is currently the only objective; a variance guard belongs next to it.

awaiting_your_choice.title: Track the results column after the events run
awaiting_your_choice.what: The official page has a Results column that is empty before the event; capture it afterwards into a results table.
awaiting_your_choice.why: Field sizes turn the descriptive ratio into an actual measured overlay rate for next year's trip.

awaiting_your_choice.title: Alert policy
awaiting_your_choice.what: Decide what a 'changed' source should do: commit only (today's behaviour), or also open an issue / send a mail.
awaiting_your_choice.why: A silent daily commit is easy to miss while you are deciding where to stay (FG-17).
